statusDefinitions.label: Available in alpha
statusDefinitions.description: Usable in the current alpha build, with further refinement still expected.

statusDefinitions.label: In testing
statusDefinitions.description: Implemented far enough for active validation, but not presented as production-ready.

statusDefinitions.label: In development
statusDefinitions.description: Actively being built or completed for the public beta product.

statusDefinitions.label: Planned
statusDefinitions.description: Approved direction, but not available in the current alpha.

statusDefinitions.label: Future
statusDefinitions.description: A direction being explored rather than a launch promise.

phases.title: Alpha / V1 Completion
phases.summary: Shieldwall is finishing and testing the complete Mimir public-beta product: the connected local worldbuilding foundation, deeper creative tools, migration, Proving Grounds, collaboration and hosting.
phases.milestone: The work here leads to a feature-complete public commercial beta, not a small closed test.

features.name: Structured worldbuilding core
features.shortDescription: Connected editors for characters, places, cultures, factions, events, languages, quests and more.
features.detail: Mimir already provides the local foundation for authoring structured entries in readable files. V1 work continues to bring the full editor set and connected workflows to launch quality.
features.whyItMatters: A structured source of truth lets the same canon power browsing, visualisation, validation, AI and interactive testing.

features.name: Links, backlinks & relationships
features.shortDescription: Connect entries directly and follow those relationships throughout the world.
features.detail: Wiki-links, backlinks and maintained inverse relationships already connect world entries instead of leaving them as isolated pages.
features.whyItMatters: The value of a world lives in the connections between its people, places, histories and ideas.

features.name: Trees & visual structures
features.shortDescription: See family, species, culture, faction and place structures as connected visual systems.
features.detail: Tree tooling is already part of the alpha foundation, with V1 expanding the range and finish of the visual structures used across the world.
features.whyItMatters: Visual structures reveal patterns and gaps that are difficult to spot in prose alone.

features.name: Timeline & calendar
features.shortDescription: Define an in-world calendar and understand events across the world's chronology.
features.detail: The alpha includes timeline and calendar foundations, including custom world chronology. V1 work continues around breadth, polish and connected navigation.
features.whyItMatters: Chronology keeps ages, reigns, journeys, conflicts and narrative arcs internally coherent.

features.name: Validation, history & accessibility
features.shortDescription: Catch structural issues, recover earlier work and adapt the interface to different reading needs.
features.detail: Validation warnings, Git-backed history and rollback, keyboard support and dyslexia-first accessibility controls are present in the alpha foundation and continue to be refined.
features.whyItMatters: A serious creative tool should help protect the work and remain usable for the people creating it.

features.name: Interactive maps
features.shortDescription: Connect locations and entries to geography rather than keeping place trapped in prose.
features.detail: Maps are part of the V1 Core scope and are being completed alongside the other connected visual tools.
features.whyItMatters: Spatial context helps creators understand travel, borders, influence and the physical consequences of world events.

features.name: Narrative tools
features.shortDescription: Plan story arcs, quests and dialogue beside the lore they depend on.
features.detail: Story Arc, Quest and Dialogue editors are part of the complete V1 product, with Narrative Planner and deeper workflows progressing through the paid tiers.
features.whyItMatters: Narrative work stays connected to canon instead of becoming a second disconnected planning system.

features.name: Mimir AI
features.shortDescription: Ask questions against relevant world context without treating unsupported invention as canon.
features.detail: The development build contains Mimir AI workflows. Production work is focused on grounded retrieval, uncertainty, routing and a customer-facing credit system rather than provider-model selection.
features.whyItMatters: Creators can understand a large world faster while keeping the distinction between written canon and inference visible.

features.name: Lore Consistency Review
features.shortDescription: Surface contradictions that deterministic validation cannot understand on its own.
features.detail: Lore Consistency Review is being built as a deeper Worldsmith workflow for conflicting dates, relationships and facts across connected canon.
features.whyItMatters: Contradictions become harder to spot as a world grows and can undermine stories, campaigns and production.

features.name: Constructed-language Translator
features.shortDescription: Translate against grammar, vocabulary, registers and writing systems defined by the creator.
features.detail: Translator is included across the planned V1 tiers within each tier's Mimir AI credit allowance. Current implementation remains under validation for the public beta.
features.whyItMatters: A constructed language stays consistent with its authored rules instead of becoming disconnected flavour text.

features.name: General import & competitor migration
features.shortDescription: Bring existing files and projects into a local Mimir world without rebuilding everything by hand.
features.detail: Ordinary import and competitor migration are being completed as Core capabilities. The production flow will let users review mappings and warnings before committing the migration.
features.whyItMatters: Changing tools should not require abandoning years of worldbuilding or paying for permission to keep it.

features.name: Proving Grounds
features.shortDescription: Prototype conversations, quests, tabletop sessions and interactive ideas against the same world data.
features.detail: Proving Grounds is approved V1 scope and is planned for the feature-complete public beta. It is not presented as available in the current alpha.
features.whyItMatters: Worldbuilders can test what happens next without separating experimentation from their canonical source material.

features.name: Simulation & world-state systems
features.shortDescription: Use variables, conditions and state to test how interactive structures behave.
features.detail: Simulation and world-state tooling are being developed for the Worldsmith tier and deeper Proving Grounds workflows.
features.whyItMatters: Creators can explore consequences before committing an idea to canon or production.

features.name: Collaboration & hosted worlds
features.shortDescription: Create shared workspaces and controlled player or participant experiences.
features.detail: Collaboration, hosted worlds and live hosted Proving Grounds are approved V1 scope but remain planned for the public-beta product. Core users will be able to accept invitations within the host's allowance.
features.whyItMatters: One power user can build and host without requiring every collaborator or player to subscribe.

features.name: Launch QA, reliability & access
features.shortDescription: Remove obvious friction and strengthen keyboard, visual, performance and recovery behaviour.
features.detail: The alpha period includes focused bug removal, accessibility checks, packaging, reliability work and validation of the complete launch suite.
features.whyItMatters: Public beta must be a usable commercial release rather than a feature list held together by caveats.

phases.title: Public Beta
phases.summary: Public beta is the first real commercial Mimir release: the complete Core and paid-tier suite, production account and commerce infrastructure, public downloads, onboarding and hosted services.
phases.milestone: Alpha now, then a feature-complete public commercial beta, then deliberate growth and stabilisation.

features.name: Complete Core + paid-tier suite
features.shortDescription: Ship the approved V1 capability progression across Core, Apprentice, Worldsmith and Loremaster.
features.detail: The public beta opens when the planned V1 feature suite is coherent enough to offer as a real product, with Core remaining permanently useful and paid tiers adding capability and hosted scale.
features.whyItMatters: Beta users need to evaluate the genuine product and commercial model, not a narrow teaser build.

features.name: Production accounts & entitlements
features.shortDescription: Create the account, tier and ownership foundation needed for commercial use.
features.detail: Production authentication, account records and entitlements are required to manage tiers, credits, owned packs and hosted access with minimal retained customer data.
features.whyItMatters: The application needs a reliable record of what each customer can use without compromising local ownership.

features.name: Subscriptions & payments
features.shortDescription: Enable the planned paid tiers through production Stripe subscription handling inside Mimir.
features.detail: Paid checkout is not live during alpha. Public beta requires subscriptions, billing state and cancellation or downgrade handling aligned with the approved tier model.
features.whyItMatters: Commercial availability requires clear, trustworthy billing without changing ownership of local work.

features.name: Production Mimir AI credits
features.shortDescription: Replace development quota stubs with customer-facing allowances, estimates and reliable accounting.
features.detail: Mimir will route processing internally. Public beta requires production credit balances, monthly resets, top-up handling and protection from charges caused by Shieldwall-side failures.
features.whyItMatters: Users need to understand and control AI usage without learning provider pricing or model menus.

features.name: Hosted collaboration infrastructure
features.shortDescription: Provide production sync, permissions, storage and realtime services for invited shared worlds.
features.detail: The public beta requires the infrastructure behind collaborative workspaces, hosted participant worlds and live Proving Grounds, with limits applying only to Shieldwall-hosted resources.
features.whyItMatters: Shared experiences must be dependable without placing artificial limits on local worlds.

features.name: Public download & install flow
features.shortDescription: Move from a waitlist to signed, understandable installer delivery for supported desktop platforms.
features.detail: At public beta the primary website action changes from Join the beta to Download Mimir, with release information, requirements and appropriate installer delivery.
features.whyItMatters: A commercial beta must be directly usable rather than accessible only through a mailing list.

features.name: Commercial beta onboarding
features.shortDescription: Guide new worldbuilders from installation to their first useful connected world.
features.detail: The launch onboarding must explain local files, world creation, migration, Core capabilities and optional online services without overwhelming new users.
features.whyItMatters: The first session should demonstrate Mimir's value before complexity becomes friction.

features.name: Production migration flow
features.shortDescription: Ship the reviewed import and migration experience as a dependable Core path.
features.detail: Public beta migration must support real source projects, clear mapping review, warnings and a safe local result rather than an opaque one-click promise.
features.whyItMatters: The ability to bring established work is central to Mimir's launch proposition.

features.name: Launch QA & reliability
features.shortDescription: Validate the full suite, packaging, accessibility, hosted allowances and recovery paths.
features.detail: Before public beta, Shieldwall must complete obvious bug removal, installer checks, workload benchmarking, hosted load testing and end-to-end reliability review.
features.whyItMatters: The public beta is a genuine release and must earn confidence across both local and online workflows.

features.name: Founder early-adopter programme
features.shortDescription: Recognise accounts created during the first six months of public beta with approved historical benefits.
features.detail: The programme is approved for public beta launch, not active during alpha. It includes a permanent Founder badge and extra Core AI credits, with separate Founding Member content-pack benefits after the retained-paid condition.
features.whyItMatters: It recognises early customers without inventing fake urgency or permanently discounting subscriptions.

phases.title: Stabilisation & Community
phases.summary: After beta, Shieldwall deliberately learns from real users. The priority becomes onboarding, migration, reliability, accessibility and the quality of the workflows already shipped before another wave of major features.
phases.milestone: Feedback leads the work here. This phase is not a race to pile on unrelated features.

features.name: Onboarding refinement
features.shortDescription: Use activation and support evidence to remove friction from the first Mimir sessions.
features.detail: Real user behaviour will shape first-run guidance, world setup, feature discovery and the path from download to a useful connected world.
features.whyItMatters: A powerful product only helps when people can reach its value quickly and confidently.

features.name: Migration refinement
features.shortDescription: Improve source coverage, mapping, warnings and review from real migration attempts.
features.detail: Post-beta migration work responds to actual source formats, edge cases and user expectations rather than assuming every project behaves alike.
features.whyItMatters: Trust is won when long-established worlds arrive intact and understandable.

features.name: Proving Grounds refinement
features.shortDescription: Expand the interactive workflows that writers, GMs and designers actually use.
features.detail: Choices, state, session tools and scenario workflows will be refined after creators can test them in real projects.
features.whyItMatters: The strongest version of Proving Grounds should be shaped by use rather than assumption.

features.name: Collaboration & hosting hardening
features.shortDescription: Strengthen permissions, sync, conflicts, capacity and participant experience.
features.detail: Shared worlds will be hardened using real collaborative projects and hosted participant sessions after beta.
features.whyItMatters: Creative teams and Game Masters need predictable shared access, especially when private information and spoilers are involved.

features.name: Mimir AI retrieval & routing
features.shortDescription: Improve answer quality, context selection, latency and credit efficiency from measured workloads.
features.detail: Real questions and review operations will guide retrieval tuning, routing decisions, caching and uncertainty behaviour.
features.whyItMatters: Grounded answers depend as much on finding the right canon as on the model producing the response.

features.name: Accessibility & usability improvement
features.shortDescription: Continue keyboard, screen-reader, visual and workflow accessibility work with user feedback.
features.detail: Accessibility remains an ongoing product responsibility after launch rather than a one-time checklist.
features.whyItMatters: Worldbuilding should remain usable across different reading, motor and sensory needs.

features.name: Reliability & performance
features.shortDescription: Harden local, hosted and AI workflows using telemetry and real failure patterns.
features.detail: Post-beta work includes performance, recovery, conflict handling, packaging and operational reliability across the product.
features.whyItMatters: Creative trust grows when the tool is quiet, fast and dependable.

features.name: Feedback-led product changes
features.shortDescription: Prioritise real pain, retention friction and repeated requests over speculative feature volume.
features.detail: Shieldwall will use support evidence, structured feedback and product telemetry to decide what deserves refinement or expansion.
features.whyItMatters: The roadmap should respond to worldbuilders rather than reward the appearance of constant novelty.

features.name: Community Hub
features.shortDescription: A private account space for voting, feedback, reports, announcements, surveys, challenges and progression.
features.detail: The planned Hub includes feature and pack voting, feedback, bug reports, announcements, surveys, previews, challenges, profiles, achievements, badges and Worldbuilder Score. Competition remains private to friends and collaborators. There is no stranger discovery, open public messaging, public feed or public world-sharing network.
features.whyItMatters: Worldbuilders can help shape Mimir and discover useful product workflows without turning Mimir into a social network.

features.name: In-app store & Shieldwall content packs
features.shortDescription: Offer optional connected packs inside Mimir when the store, entitlements and launch packs are actually ready.
features.detail: Normal Mimir commerce is intended to happen inside the application. Shieldwall packs are connected worldbuilding material, not isolated text dumps, and are separate from any later third-party marketplace. No pack prices are committed here.
features.whyItMatters: Optional packs can save preparation time while keeping blank-world creation a first-class path.
features.mediaSlot: Real pack and store captures when ready

phases.title: Integrations & Ecosystem
phases.summary: Once the core product is stable, Mimir can connect the same canonical world to the wider creative toolchain through controlled AI and game-engine workflows.
phases.milestone: These are planned post-V1 integrations. None are advertised as public-beta features.

features.name: ChatGPT MCP
features.shortDescription: Let ChatGPT work with a Mimir world through controlled operations.
features.detail: A future MCP connection may allow approved read and, where appropriate, write workflows against the creator's canonical Mimir world.
features.whyItMatters: Creators would not need to repeatedly paste and maintain separate world context.

features.name: Claude MCP
features.shortDescription: Let Claude query and work with the same controlled Mimir source of truth.
features.detail: A future MCP connection may expose carefully controlled world operations without changing Mimir's local-first ownership principles.
features.whyItMatters: The same canon can support different creative tools without duplicating or drifting context.

features.name: Unreal Engine
features.shortDescription: Connect structured Mimir world and narrative data to Unreal workflows.
features.detail: The planned Unreal integration follows V1 refinement and will be defined against real production needs rather than presented as a launch entitlement.
features.whyItMatters: A canonical world can inform implementation without requiring a second manually maintained data source.

features.name: Unity
features.shortDescription: Connect Mimir's canonical world data to Unity projects and narrative systems.
features.detail: The planned Unity integration is post-V1 work and remains dependent on the stable core product and validated engine workflows.
features.whyItMatters: Narrative and world data can move closer to the systems that use it in production.

features.name: Godot
features.shortDescription: Connect Mimir world data to Godot through a workflow designed for the engine.
features.detail: The planned Godot integration is post-V1 work and will be prioritised after refinement of the public-beta product.
features.whyItMatters: The canonical world should be useful across different production stacks.

features.name: Advanced engine & data workflows
features.shortDescription: Explore export, synchronisation and eventual round-tripping between canon and implementation.
features.detail: Advanced workflows may extend beyond one-way export, but their exact shape depends on real Unreal, Unity and Godot integration needs.
features.whyItMatters: The long-term value is one dependable source of truth rather than a growing collection of brittle copies.

phases.title: Future Possibilities
phases.summary: These are directions to explore when real demand justifies them. They are intentionally less certain than the public-beta, refinement and integration work above.

features.name: Mimir Studio / business plan
features.shortDescription: A possible future plan for organisations with needs beyond ordinary creator subscriptions.
features.detail: A future business plan may be created only when professional demand justifies central billing, larger teams, administration and deployment features.
features.whyItMatters: Professional needs should be solved deliberately rather than hidden inside consumer tiers.

features.name: Organisation administration
features.shortDescription: Explore organisation-level permissions, account management, auditability and SSO.
features.detail: Advanced administration and enterprise identity features are future possibilities, not current V1 entitlements.
features.whyItMatters: Larger teams may eventually need governance beyond a normal collaborative workspace.

features.name: Professional onboarding & support
features.shortDescription: Explore paid onboarding, guaranteed support and deployment services for larger customers.
features.detail: Professional onboarding and future SLA-style support remain separate possible services rather than benefits silently bundled into consumer subscriptions.
features.whyItMatters: Organisations can receive appropriate help without raising ordinary creator pricing to fund enterprise service.

features.name: Third-party artist marketplace
features.shortDescription: Explore a later marketplace for approved artists and human-made replacement art packs.
features.detail: This is distinct from Shieldwall-created content packs. Commission, moderation, tax, refunds, seller payouts and copyright processes must be settled before any marketplace promise.
features.whyItMatters: Artists could offer optional alternatives while creators retain control over the art used in their worlds.

features.name: Session capture & extraction
features.shortDescription: Explore turning recorded design or play sessions into reviewable world and narrative updates.
features.detail: Any future capture workflow would need clear consent, review and source boundaries before changes become canon.
features.whyItMatters: Useful discoveries from play and design sessions could be easier to preserve without treating raw transcription as truth.

features.name: Further creative tooling
features.shortDescription: Leave room for new worldbuilding workflows demonstrated by real user demand.
features.detail: Future tools will be prioritised from evidence rather than filling the roadmap with speculative promises.
features.whyItMatters: Mimir can evolve with worldbuilders while keeping committed work understandable and honest.
